articles.title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 13 reports examining bronchoscopic valve placement for persistent air leak and bronchopleural fistula in children, showing potential as rescue therapy but highlighting the need for higher-quality evidence.
summary: This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception through June 2026 for studies reporting pediatric or late-adolescent patients undergoing bronchoscopic endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement for persistent air leak (PAL), bronchopleural fistula (BPF), or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Thirteen eligible reports—including case reports, case series, and observational studies—were included with data extracted independently by two reviewers.

Valve placement resulted in rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children across diverse clinical contexts: necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue formation, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumotharax, and recurrent air leak, though many children underwent uncomplicated valve removal.

The authors conclude that endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may serve as rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF, but acknowledge that evidence remains low-certainty due to small sample sizes, retrospective study design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. They emphasize the need for prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting to clarify patient selection, optimal timing, and safety.
articles.why: Persistent air leak and bronchopleural fistula are uncommon but serious complications in pediatric populations, particularly in the context of severe pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or critical illness requiring ECMO. This review identifies valve placement as a potential minimally invasive alternative to surgery when conservative management fails or surgical risk is prohibitive. Clinicians managing refractory air leak in children might use this summary to contextualize valve placement within current evidence and recognize the lack of standardized protocols.
articles.evidence: Thirteen reports including case reports, case series, and observational studies (exact sample sizes not stated in abstract). Design was retrospective across most included studies. Major limitations include small patient numbers per report, inconsistent definitions and reporting of outcomes, retrospective rather than prospective methodology, and probable publication bias. No randomized trials or prospective comparative studies are indicated. The abstract does not provide an aggregate sample size or detailed breakdown by study type.

articles.title: Medication non-adherence and its associated factors among heart failure patients in Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 17 African studies found that approximately 42% of heart failure patients do not adhere to prescribed medications, with lack of health insurance being the strongest associated factor.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized observational studies published between 2000 and 2025 reporting medication non-adherence among heart failure patients across Africa. Seventeen studies encompassing 6,276 patients were included. Study quality was assessed using standardized critical appraisal checklists, and data were pooled using random-effects modeling.

The pooled prevalence of medication non-adherence was 41.88% (95% CI: 25.43–58.34), with substantial regional variation—Western Africa showed the highest rate at 77.59%. Lack of health insurance emerged as the strongest predictor of non-adherence (OR = 4.27), followed by polypharmacy (OR = 2.58) and presence of comorbidities (OR = 1.76).

The authors conclude that approximately two in five heart failure patients in Africa are non-adherent to medications, driven by financial, clinical, and therapy-related barriers. They recommend multi-faceted regional interventions including expanded health insurance coverage, medication subsidies, simplification of complex regimens, and context-specific adherence support tailored to local healthcare systems.
articles.why: Medication non-adherence significantly worsens heart failure outcomes. This review identifies that adherence challenges in Africa are predominantly linked to health insurance access and medication complexity—factors amenable to health system and policy intervention rather than solely patient behavior. Understanding regional variation and specific barriers may help inform advocacy, resource allocation, and design of locally appropriate support strategies across African healthcare settings.
articles.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies (cross-sectional and cohort designs). Sample: 6,276 patients across 17 studies. Major limitations: extreme heterogeneity (I² = 99.7%), indicating substantial between-study variation not fully explained by regional subgroup analyses alone. The range of adherence estimates (95% CI: 25.43–58.34) reflects this uncertainty. Definitions of non-adherence and measurement methods likely varied across included studies. No publication bias was detected by Egger's test (p = 0.267). Full-text methodology details and reasons for heterogeneity are not available from the abstract.

articles.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 105 studies found that malignancy was associated with higher mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock, with the strength of association varying by timing of death measurement and cancer type.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined all-cause mortality differences between sepsis patients with and without malignancy across multiple studies. Researchers searched five major databases through September 2025 and identified 105 eligible studies involving over 20 million participants; 85 studies contributed 101 mortality endpoint estimates to the primary analysis. Mortality outcomes were stratified by timing: ICU, in-hospital, early (unspecified duration), intermediate, and extended follow-up periods.

Pooled analyses showed elevated mortality odds ratios across all endpoints: ICU mortality (OR 1.21), in-hospital (OR 1.90), early (OR 1.81), intermediate (OR 2.28), and extended follow-up (OR 2.41). The association was sustained for hematologic malignancy, concentrated in in-hospital and early mortality for metastatic disease, and more modest for solid tumors. Sensitivity analyses generally showed directional consistency, though risk ratio estimates were smaller than odds ratios.

The authors note these represent unadjusted, overall prognostic associations rather than independent causal effects, as studies were not adjusted for potential confounders. Exploratory meta-regression suggested that severity-related covariates may explain some variation in findings across studies. The findings support the need for endpoint-specific prognostic assessment when evaluating sepsis outcomes in cancer patients.
articles.why: Sepsis in patients with malignancy represents a high-risk clinical scenario with complex prognostic implications. These findings suggest that cancer type and stage matter: outcomes differ between hematologic versus solid tumors and between metastatic versus localized disease. Clinicians and prognostication discussions may benefit from recognizing that mortality risk varies substantially depending on when outcomes are assessed—differences between ICU and in-hospital mortality were notably large. However, because published estimates are largely unadjusted, they may reflect differences in disease severity, performance status, or treatment intensity rather than cancer itself independently worsening sepsis outcomes.
articles.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies. Total sample of over 20 million participants across 105 studies, with 85 studies (101 endpoints) contributing to primary synthesis. Major limitations: (1) results are unadjusted estimates, meaning confounding by severity of sepsis, cancer stage, performance status, and treatment decisions cannot be excluded; (2) substantial heterogeneity across studies, partially explored via meta-regression but not fully explained; (3) granular cancer characteristics (histology, stage, treatment status) were not consistently available; (4) publication dates and specific study designs not detailed in abstract; (5) reasons for heterogeneity between odds ratio and risk ratio estimates unexplained. Confidence intervals crossed the null for ICU mortality only.

articles.title: Surgical outcomes and functional morbidity after retrosigmoid/retrocondylar and midline suboccipital approaches for foramen magnum meningiomas: a single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.dek: Posterior and posterolateral surgical approaches for foramen magnum meningiomas achieve high resection rates and low recurrence with acceptable morbidity, according to a meta-analysis of seven retrospective case series.
summary: This single-arm meta-analysis pooled data from seven retrospective case series (1997–2019) totaling 133 patients with foramen magnum meningiomas treated via retrosigmoid/retrocondylar approaches (55.6%) or midline suboccipital craniectomy (44.4%), often combined with C1 laminectomy. The weighted mean age was 54.4 years, 75.2% were female, and mean follow-up was 58 months. Retrosigmoid/retrocondylar corridors were used predominantly for anterior/anterolateral tumors, whereas midline approaches addressed mixed attachment sites.

Pooled gross total resection was 91% (95% CI: 84–96%), with recurrence in only 1% (3 of 133 patients). Long-term functional independence was achieved in 83% (95% CI: 71–93%) of the subset with available data. New cranial nerve deficits (transient or permanent) occurred in 21%, cerebrospinal fluid leak in 12%, and perioperative mortality in 3%; two additional deaths from aspiration pneumonia occurred during follow-up. When condyle drilling was performed, it was generally limited to the posterior one-third, and no postoperative craniocervical instability or fusion was reported.

The authors conclude that these less extensive posterior and posterolateral approaches achieve favorable oncologic control and functional outcomes without extensive condylectomy. However, they emphasize that formal approach-specific comparisons were limited by heterogeneous reporting, and that the two approaches are applied to anatomically distinct tumors and should not be considered interchangeable. Cranial nerve morbidity, cerebrospinal fluid leak, and perioperative mortality remain important considerations when counseling patients.
articles.why: Foramen magnum meningiomas present a surgical management dilemma: their location near critical neural and vascular structures demands careful approach selection. This meta-analysis provides pooled estimates of outcomes with less extensive posterior approaches, which may inform perioperative risk discussions and operative planning. The finding of high resection rates with acceptable morbidity suggests that these approaches merit consideration, particularly for tumors with posterior or posterolateral attachments; however, the heterogeneity of tumor location and reporting across studies limits direct comparison of approaches and generalizability to all patient presentations.
articles.evidence: Single-arm meta-analysis of seven retrospective case series; no randomized controlled trials or prospective cohort studies. Total sample 133 eligible patients, though one series contributed only 34 of its larger cohort. Major limitations include: retrospective design and risk of selection bias in all contributing studies; heterogeneous reporting of outcomes, precluding formal approach-specific comparisons; different tumor topographies treated by each approach (anterior/anterolateral vs. posterior/posterolateral), conflating approach-specific effects; small numbers for some outcomes (e.g., only 3 recurrences, 7 perioperative deaths); limited long-term follow-up data for functional status (60 of 74 patients with data); and absence of information on skull base instability assessment methods. The meta-analysis does not separate outcomes by approach, limiting inference about comparative effectiveness. Confidence intervals for rare outcomes are wide, reflecting uncertainty.

articles.title: Risk of retinal vascular occlusion following COVID-19 vaccination: A meta-analysis of nearly 15 million individuals.
articles.dek: A meta-analysis of nearly 15 million individuals found retinal vascular occlusion was rare after COVID-19 vaccination, though separate analyses of arterial and venous subtypes showed statistically significant associations.
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined five observational studies reporting 14,877,781 vaccinated participants to assess the frequency and risk of retinal vascular occlusion (RVO) following COVID-19 vaccination. The pooled proportion of RVO events among vaccinated individuals was 0.02% (95% CI: 0.00%–0.07%).

The overall association between vaccination and RVO was not statistically significant (RR = 2.12, 95% CI: 0.65–6.90; P = .213). However, when analyzed separately, retinal artery occlusion showed a significant association (RR = 2.03, 95% CI: 1.17–3.51) and retinal vein occlusion also showed significance (RR = 2.26, 95% CI: 2.08–2.47). For vaccine types, only ChAdOx1/AstraZeneca showed a significant association (RR = 2.00, 95% CI: 1.60–2.50), based on a single contributing study.

The authors conclude that RVO events following COVID-19 vaccination were rare events overall. They note that substantial heterogeneity between studies, potential confounding factors, and differences in study designs limit definitive causal conclusions, and they call for further research to clarify these findings.
articles.why: Retinal vascular occlusion is a serious but rare vision-threatening condition. These findings may be relevant to clinicians counseling patients about vaccine safety profiles and to those evaluating visual complaints temporally associated with vaccination. The discordance between the nonsignificant overall association and significant subtype-specific associations highlights the importance of careful outcome definition and suggests that clinician awareness of RVO as a rare potential signal warrants continued monitoring, while the rarity of the event (0.02%) should contextualize risk discussions.
articles.evidence: Observational study design (meta-analysis of five studies). Sample size: 14,877,781 reported participants. Major limitations include: substantial heterogeneity (I² = 96.8% for overall analysis; I² = 99.5% for pooled proportions), potential overlapping study populations that were assessed but not fully resolved, inability to control for confounding factors inherent to observational data, reliance on a single study for vaccine-type-specific conclusions (ChAdOx1/AstraZeneca), and wide confidence intervals for the overall estimate. The authors explicitly state these factors limit definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Comparison of the Safety and Efficacy of Remimazolam for Sedation in Adults Undergoing Fiberoptic Bronchoscopy: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.dek: A meta-analysis of 16 randomized controlled trials comparing remimazolam to other sedatives for fiberoptic bronchoscopy found reduced respiratory depression, hypotension, and bradycardia with comparable procedural success and faster recovery.
summary: This meta-analysis synthesized data from 16 randomized controlled trials involving 2,325 adults undergoing fiberoptic bronchoscopy. The analysis compared remimazolam, a novel ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, against dexmedetomidine, midazolam, and propofol across multiple safety and efficacy outcomes including respiratory depression, hemodynamic effects, sedation timing, procedure success, emergence time, and postoperative care unit duration.

Remimazolam significantly reduced the incidence of respiratory depression (relative risk 0.51), hypotension (relative risk 0.50), and bradycardia (relative risk 0.37) compared with control sedatives. Onset of sedation was 2.19 minutes faster than dexmedetomidine but 0.49 minutes slower than propofol. Procedure success rates were similar across all groups. Emergence time was shorter after remimazolam compared with dexmedetomidine (1.79 minutes faster) and midazolam (4.37 minutes faster), with corresponding reductions in postoperative care unit stay.

The authors conclude that remimazolam offers effective sedation for fiberoptic bronchoscopy with favorable safety and recovery profiles. These findings suggest potential advantages for patient comfort and hemodynamic stability, though the clinical magnitude of differences in timing outcomes and real-world applicability require consideration.
articles.why: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy requires sedation that balances patient comfort with preservation of spontaneous respiration and cardiovascular stability. The respiratory depression and hemodynamic complications associated with traditional sedatives can complicate procedures. This analysis contributes to the evidence base for remimazolam as an alternative, which could inform clinician discussions about sedative selection, particularly for patients at higher risk for respiratory or hemodynamic compromise. However, comparative effectiveness in specific high-risk populations and cost-effectiveness have not been addressed in this abstract.
articles.evidence: Design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials through January 2026. Sample: 16 RCTs enrolling 2,325 patients total. Limitations and uncertainties: The abstract does not specify the number of trials for each drug comparison, variation in trial quality assessment methods, heterogeneity in sedation protocols or dosing across included trials, or whether adverse event definitions were standardized across studies. The clinical significance of differences in emergence time (measured in minutes) and PACU stay relative to procedural duration is unclear. Publication bias assessment is not mentioned. Longer-term safety outcomes beyond the immediate perioperative period are not addressed.

articles.title: Effect of Kunxian capsule, a novel Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, on reducing proteinuria and slowing renal function decline in diabetic kidney disease: a 48-week randomized controlled trial.
articles.dek: A 48-week randomized controlled trial found that adding Kunxian capsule, a Tripterygium wilfordii preparation, to irbesartan reduced proteinuria and slowed kidney function decline in patients with diabetic kidney disease.
summary: Eighty patients with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) were randomly assigned to receive either standard therapy with irbesartan plus Kunxian capsule (experimental group, n=40) or irbesartan alone (control group, n=40) for 48 weeks. The trial evaluated proteinuria remission, reduction in 24-hour urinary protein, kidney function decline, and safety.

The experimental group showed a higher proteinuria remission rate (57.50% vs. 25.00%), shorter median time to remission (5 months vs. not reached), greater reduction in 24-hour urinary protein, and lower incidence of renal composite hard endpoint (10.00% vs. 32.50%) compared to control. The experimental group also demonstrated slower eGFR decline and significant reductions in inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate). No significant differences in adverse events were observed between groups.

The authors conclude that Kunxian capsule as an adjunctive therapy to irbesartan may improve proteinuria remission and attenuate renal function decline in DKD patients. These findings suggest potential clinical utility, though the clinical significance of individual outcome measures and generalizability require further examination.
articles.why: DKD remains inadequately controlled despite renin-angiotensin system blockade in many patients. If confirmed, adjunctive herbal therapy with demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties could offer an additional treatment option for slowing kidney disease progression. Results merit discussion regarding mechanisms of proteinuria reduction and whether anti-inflammatory effects contribute to kidney protection, as well as consideration of larger and longer-term studies.
articles.evidence: Randomized controlled trial with 80 patients total (40 per group) over 48 weeks. Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04981613, registered March 2, 2021). Limitations include modest sample size, relatively short follow-up duration, lack of reported confidence intervals or p-values in the abstract, unclear blinding status, and absence of information regarding baseline comparability, dropout rates, and whether the renal composite hard endpoint definition was prespecified. The abstract does not specify whether intent-to-treat analysis was primary or whether there was protocol deviation. Generalizability to other populations and healthcare settings is uncertain.

articles.title: Pulmonary Embolism Response Teams: Evolution of Guidelines, Our Institutional Model and Systematic Review of Published Literature.
articles.dek: A systematic review examining the evolution of pulmonary embolism response team models and guideline recommendations for managing intermediate-high and high-risk PE presentations.
summary: This article reviews the development and implementation of Pulmonary Embolism Response Teams (PERTs) as a multidisciplinary care model. The authors summarize evolving evidence and guideline recommendations that have shaped contemporary PE management, focusing on cases presenting with intermediate-high or high-risk features characterized by right ventricular failure from increased pulmonary vascular resistance.

The review addresses a recognized gap in clinical guidance: despite advances in imaging and therapeutic technology, management strategies for PE requiring escalation beyond anticoagulation remain inconsistent across institutions. The PERT model was developed to standardize decision-making through real-time multidisciplinary evaluation and individualized treatment selection.

The authors synthesize published literature on PERT models to illustrate how institutional approaches have evolved and how contemporary guidelines now inform PE care decisions. Specific numerical outcomes and comparative effectiveness data are not detailed in the available abstract.
articles.why: PE continues as a substantial cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review may inform institutional discussions about structuring multidisciplinary teams for complex PE cases and understanding current guideline evolution. Clinicians managing intermediate-high or high-risk PE may benefit from understanding PERT frameworks, though this summary does not constitute practice guidance.

evidence.design: Systematic review of published literature combined with institutional model description
evidence.major_limitations: Abstract does not specify search methodology, inclusion criteria, number of studies reviewed, quality assessment approach, or comparative outcomes. No numerical results are provided regarding PERT effectiveness or guideline recommendations. Full-text review needed to evaluate evidence quality and completeness.

articles.title: Risk factors for cognitive impairment in patients undergoing hemodialysis: an umbrella review and meta-analysis.
articles.dek: An umbrella review identified multiple demographic, clinical, and dialysis-related factors associated with cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty in hemodialysis patients, though most evidence remains low certainty.
summary: This umbrella review and meta-analysis synthesized five prior meta-analyses examining risk factors for cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty in adults on maintenance hemodialysis. The analysis evaluated 97 associations from studies indexed in PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library through January 2026.

For cognitive impairment, increased risk was associated with older age, female sex, diabetes, cerebrovascular disease, multiple comorbidities, impaired physical performance, lower hemoglobin, and inflammatory markers. Higher educational attainment was protective (OR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.13–0.34). For cognitive frailty, increased risk factors included older age, female sex, depression (OR = 4.66), stroke history (OR = 2.94), comorbidities, malnutrition, longer dialysis duration (OR = 2.30), low-flux hemodialysis (OR = 4.16), and interdialytic hypotension (OR = 2.42). Higher education and serum albumin were protective.

The authors concluded that cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty are distinct outcomes with overlapping but separate risk factor profiles. Only two associations achieved moderate-certainty evidence; the remainder were rated low or very low certainty. The authors called for high-quality prospective studies to strengthen the evidence base.
articles.why: Cognitive dysfunction is common in hemodialysis populations and may inform clinical monitoring and counseling. Identifying modifiable factors (hemoglobin, albumin, dialysis modality, interdialytic hypotension) and non-modifiable demographic characteristics could help clinicians recognize vulnerable patients and discuss cognitive screening. The distinction between cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty as separate syndromes may guide how these conditions are assessed and managed, though the low certainty of most evidence limits firm recommendations.
articles.evidence: Design: Umbrella review (systematic overview of meta-analyses). Sample size not reported for the umbrella review; five included meta-analyses involved 97 total associations. Major limitations: most included associations were rated low or very low certainty; the abstract does not specify the number of original primary studies, overall hemodialysis population size, or reasons for low-certainty ratings. Whether studies were observational or included randomized trials is not stated. Publication bias assessment is not mentioned. The review synthesizes published meta-analyses rather than conducting a de novo analysis.
